tagline: Somebody's narrating dinner. Make it sound good.

    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersHam and cheddar toastiesPan-toasted leg ham and cheddar sandwiches, cut into trianglesHow to make it8 slices of white bread30g butter150g leg ham150g cheddarButter the outsides of the slices of bread and fill the sandwiches with the ham and the grated cheddar.Cook in a pan over medium heat for exactly 3 minutes a side and cut into neat triangles.Ana's bakery cheddar and chive sconesHarold came to audit her. Ana only paid the taxes she agreed withHow to make it160g butter450g self-raising flour1 tsp salt1 pinch cayenne pepper150g vintage cheddar1 bunch chives300ml full cream milkRub 60g cold butter into the flour, salt and cayenne.Stir in 120g grated cheddar and half the chives, snipped, then the milk to a soft dough.Pat 3cm thick, cut 8 rounds, brush with milk and top with the rest of the cheddar.Bake at 220°C until risen and golden.Whip the rest of the butter soft and serve with the warm scones.MainsHarold's tax audit pot pieChicken thigh and leek in creamy sauce under a puff pastry lidHow to make it800g chicken thighs2 leeks30g butter2 tbsp plain flour300ml chicken stock100ml thickened cream1 sheet puff pastry1 eggCook the diced chicken thigh with the sliced leeks in the butter.Stir in the flour, the chicken stock and the cream and simmer 10 minutes.Spoon into a dish, top with puff pastry, brush with egg and bake at 200°C for 25 minutes.Professor Hilbert's lemon pepper fishHilbert, the literature professor who sits the lifeguard chair at the campus poolHow to make it4 barramundi fillets, skin on60g butter, softened1 lemon1 tsp cracked black pepper800g small potatoes2 tbsp olive oil150g mixed salad leaves1 Lebanese cucumber1 tbsp white wine vinegarBoil the potatoes for 18 minutes, drain and crush lightly with a fork and 1 tbsp of the oil.Mash the butter with the lemon zest, pepper and a pinch of salt.Score the fish skin, salt it and cook skin side down in the rest of the oil for 5 minutes until crisp, then flip for 2 minutes.Toss the leaves and sliced cucumber with the vinegar and a squeeze of lemon.Top the fish with the lemon pepper butter and serve with the potatoes and salad.SweetsAna's three-flour brown butter cookiesThank God for Bavarian sugar cookies. Brown butter, vanilla.How to make it150g butter100g brown sugar50g caster sugar1 eggvanilla extract, to taste100g plain flour60g spelt flour40g rye flour1 tsp baking powder40g demerara sugarsea salt flakes, to tasteBrown the butter until nutty and cool 10 minutes.Whisk with the brown sugar, the caster sugar, the egg and the vanilla.Stir in the plain flour, the spelt flour, the rye flour, the baking powder and a pinch of salt.Chill 30 minutes.Heat the oven to 180°C.Roll into balls, roll in demerara sugar and bake 11 to 12 minutes.Sprinkle with flaky salt while warm.DrinksCold vanilla malted milkCold milk with vanilla bean, malt powder and honey in frosted glassesHow to make it1 vanilla bean5 tbsp malted milk powder1 tbsp honey1 L full cream milkPut the tall glasses in the freezer for 20 minutes.Scrape the seeds from half a vanilla bean into a jug.Add the malted milk powder, the honey and the milk and whisk into a smooth paste.Add the very cold full cream milk and whisk hard, or blend for 20 seconds, until frothy.Pour into the frosted glasses and dust with a little more malt.
